title: Image comparison results
description: One run of the image comparison: the plan declared before the first round, every round as measured, and the paired analysis. Written by rhvp_compare after every round to <results root>/<run.id>/results.json (on OpenShift the results volume, mounted at /results); `run.status` says whether the run finished and `run.error_code` why it did not. Times are UTC (RFC 3339); durations are seconds unless the key says ms. Side A is the baseline, side B the candidate; every ratio is B/A. $defs/status describes the separate status.json document (ConfigMap compare-<run id>).

schema.description: The schema name and major version. A reader checks it first.

id.description: runName plus the first 8 hex digits of the config's sha256: a changed config is a new run.

status.description: complete: every planned round finished, with every load level usable; partial: the run ended with failed or missing rounds, or with load levels where requests failed; failed: the run stopped on an error before the end; running: still going, or the runner died (see finished_at).

error_code.description: null when every planned round finished. ROUNDS_FAILED: every round ran and some failed (partial); REQUESTS_FAILED: every round ran, but at some load level of some round requests failed or none finished, and that level is left out (partial); STOPPED: stopped by SIGTERM, for example a deleted Job (partial); RUN_TIMEOUT: stopped near the Job's time limit (partial); RUNNER_FAILED: the run failed outside a round, for example before the first one (failed). A config that cannot be run (PLAN_INVALID), and a run that found another comparison running (RUN_ACTIVE), write no results file; those codes appear only in the log summary and the termination message.

server_restored.description: Whether the live server the backend took away for the run is back: on OpenShift the pattern's server Deployment scaled back (and read back), under docker the container named in RHVP_COMPARE_SERVER_CONTAINER started again. null when nothing was taken away (or not yet asked back); false makes the runner exit 4.

synthetic.description: true only in made-up example files (the notebook's REPLAY file); such a file is not a measurement.

gpu.description: The GPU the sides ran on, from the node's GPU feature labels (OpenShift) or nvidia-smi (docker).

nodes.description: Every node and GPU a round ran on, in the order first seen (node and gpu above keep the first). More than one node makes every verdict INCONCLUSIVE.

rounds.description: Measured rounds in run order. A round that failed is kept with its error.

analysis.description: Recomputed from plan and rounds after every round, by rhvp_compare.analyze or any tool that writes the same shape.

env.description: The side's extra environment variables, as the config gives them (sides[].env). At each start they are set after the preset's own, with {model_id} and the other placeholders filled in; what the server process saw is in each round's launches.

compile_cache.description: sides[].compileCache: cold, a fresh /cache at every start; warm (docker only), a volume kept for the run and filled by the side's warm-up round. Missing in results written before it existed (cold).

image_digest.description: repository@sha256:..., as the node pulled it.

source.description: endpoint: GET /version; log: the server's start-up log.

unit.description: share is a fraction from 0 to 1.

kind.description: Picks the verdict words: FASTER/SLOWER for speed, MORE_EFFICIENT/LESS_EFFICIENT for efficiency.

role.description: primary: in the corrected family (plan.analysis.primary); secondary: the same test, interval and tie band with an uncorrected p-value, so its verdict is descriptive.

plan.description: Everything fixed before the first round, so the metric family, test, correction, alpha and tie band are on record as declared.

mode.description: Set only in mode scaleout (the scale round); a plan without it is mode pairs.

primary.description: The primary metric ids, declared before the first round.

metrics.description: Every metric the run reports, in report order; the correction counts only the primary ones.

floor.description: The smallest adjusted p-value the planned pairs can give a primary metric (all pairs one way): when it is above alpha no primary metric can be FASTER or SLOWER. family_size is the number of primary metrics.

scale_out.description: Mode scaleout only: the scale round's settings, fixed before the first round.

request_rate.description: Requests per second of the surge (GuideLLM's constant profile).

step_after_s.description: The forced step: the second replica is asked for this long after the surge's first request reached the router.

slo.description: The latency goals GuideLLM scores each request against; tpot_ms is compared with the request's inter-token latency.

method.description: energy_counter: from the DCGM total-energy counter over the window; power_mean: the mean of the power samples in the window.

level.description: One concurrency level of one round, from GuideLLM's report; in mode scaleout, the round's one surge (concurrency null).

output_tokens_per_s.description: Over the level's window, all requests (incomplete ones at the end included), as GuideLLM's server throughput.

usable.description: false when any request errored or none finished; the level's figures then stay out of the comparison.

rate.description: Mode scaleout: the requests per second the surge sent at.

slo_attainment.description: Mode scaleout: GuideLLM's share of the judged requests that met every latency goal (a failed request counts as one that missed them; requests still running at the end are left out); null when it judged none.

goodput_rps.description: Mode scaleout: requests per second that met every latency goal (GuideLLM's request_goodput, mean over the successful requests).

seconds.description: A phase the server timed itself, in its own words.

at_s.description: When the line was written, in seconds since the round asked for the server (node clock).

count.description: How many lines were added up into seconds.

status.description: ok, or failed with error and error_code.

error_code.description: null when the round is ok. GPU_NOT_FREE: another pod or program still held the GPU; SIDE_FAILED: the side failed (bad image, pull failure, no node, or the server exited); SIDE_NEVER_READY: no model listed, or no answer, before the time limit; LOAD_FAILED: GuideLLM failed or timed out after its one retry, or its report is unusable; STOPPED: the runner was stopped during the round; RUNNER_ERROR: anything else (the platform's API, a fault in the runner).

ready_s.description: From just before the runner asked for the server until GET /v1/models listed the model.

first_answer_s.description: From the same moment until the first generated text of a streamed completion.

launches.description: Every server start in the round, by replica (1 for the round's first start, 2 for the replica a scale round adds).

metrics.description: The round's figure for each metric id in plan.metrics that it measured (0 or more). A 0, such as 0 output tokens per second, gives no ratio: the analysis counts that pair as lost to this side (pairs_lost). The analysis reads only this map.

artifacts.description: Paths relative to the run's folder.

server_log_attempt_1.description: The server log of the start that stopped at vLLM's start-up memory check, when the side was started again.

server_log_2_attempt_1.description: Mode scaleout: the same for the second replica, when it was started again.

guidellm_surge_1.description: Mode scaleout: GuideLLM's log of a surge that timed out and was run once more (runner.SURGE_RETRIES).

router_surge_1.description: Mode scaleout: the router's log of that first surge.

server_log_2_surge_1.description: Mode scaleout: the log of the second replica of that first surge, taken down before the surge ran again.

start_retries.description: How many times the side was started again in this round after its server stopped at vLLM's start-up memory check ('Error in memory profiling'; a GPU whose memory is the machine's own fails it when another program frees memory while it measures). Each replica is started again at most once (its launch record's start_retries); a second such failure of the same replica fails the round (SIDE_FAILED). This is the sum over the round's replicas. The first replica's start-up figures are timed from its last start; a replica that a scale-out round adds is timed from when it was first asked for, so its first try's time counts.

scale.description: Mode scaleout, a scored or A/A round that reached the forced step: the step, the second replica, and how the router shared the surge out. Times in seconds are since the surge's first request reached the router, by the runner's clock.

step_at_s.description: When the second replica was asked for (the plan's step_after_s, plus the runner's own delay).

joined_at_s.description: When the router started to send it requests.

joined_during_surge.description: false when the surge had ended before the replica answered: it got no requests.

cancelled.description: Requests whose client went away, as GuideLLM does with the requests still running when the surge ends.

new_replica_share.description: The second replica's share of the surge's requests through the router.

events.description: The rhvp-scale lines in the first replica's log (servers that write them).

load_triggered_s.description: The first scale-up the server itself logged after the surge began (metric scale.load_triggered_s).

launch.description: One start of a side's server (rhvp_compare/launch.py): what the runner asked for, and the environment the server process saw, for the allow-listed names only.

replica.description: 1 for the round's first server start; 2 and up for each replica a scale-out round adds, in start order.

started_at.description: When the runner asked for this start.

entrypoint.description: image: the image's own entrypoint ran; override: the side's command ran in its place, bypassing whatever the entrypoint sets.

command.description: The command the runner set, or null for the image's own entrypoint.

image_entrypoint.description: The image's ENTRYPOINT as its config states it; null when not read.

image_cmd.description: The image's CMD as its config states it; null when not read.

env.description: The environment the server process saw: GLIBC_TUNABLES and every name starting with CUDA_, VLLM_, TORCH_ or HF_, minus names that look like secrets.

env_source.description: process: read from the server process itself; container: the container's configured environment (image ENV plus the runner's); none: not recorded.

env_dropped.description: Allowed names left out because they look like secrets (HF_TOKEN, VLLM_API_KEY, ...); names only, never values.

start_retries.description: How many times this replica was started again in the round after its server stopped at vLLM's start-up memory check (at most once); the record describes the last start.

gpus.description: The GPU request the platform got for this start: under docker the device request ("all" or device ids, from RHVP_COMPARE_GPUS or RHVP_COMPARE_REPLICA_GPUS); a vLLM server uses the first GPU it sees. null: not recorded (OpenShift, a side without a GPU, or a file from before this field).

gpu_uuids.description: The UUIDs of the GPUs that request reached, as nvidia-smi listed them before the first round (mode scaleout). null: not read.

n_pairs.description: Pairs where both rounds measured this metric.

pairs_lost.description: Scored pairs that ran at least one round but give no ratio for this metric, by cause. A or B: only that side failed on its own account (its round failed with SIDE_FAILED, SIDE_NEVER_READY or LOAD_FAILED, requests failed at this metric's load level, or its value was 0); both: both sides did; other: any other cause (a round stopped, not run yet, the GPU not free, a missing power reading). Any A or B makes the verdict INCONCLUSIVE (reason pairs_lost_to_one_side_failing).

ratios.description: B/A per pair, in pair order.

median_ratio.description: The median of the ratios on the log scale: the middle ratio, or for an even count the geometric mean of the two middle ones, so swapping A and B gives exactly the reciprocal.

ci.description: Distribution-free interval for the median ratio (order statistics); its actual coverage is at least level, or null bounds when too few pairs.

p_sign.description: Exact two-sided sign test on the ratios (ratios of exactly 1 left out).

p_wilcoxon.description: Exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on log ratios.

p_adjusted.description: p_value after plan.analysis.correction over the primary metrics; null for a secondary metric, whose verdict uses p_value uncorrected.

reachable.description: Whether this metric's pairs could reach alpha at all: for a primary metric, the smallest corrected p-value its own number of pairs allows next to the other primary metrics' (exact for Holm and Bonferroni, a lower bound for bh); for a secondary metric, 2^(1-n).

outcome.description: B against A, in the metric's own direction.

verdict.description: The outcome in words for the metric's kind: B is FASTER/SLOWER (speed) or MORE_EFFICIENT/LESS_EFFICIENT (efficiency) than A.

reason.description: Why the verdict is what it is. TIE needs the median and its whole interval inside the tie band; FASTER/SLOWER need a corrected p-value at most alpha with the test leaning the same way as the median; the last two reasons override any other verdict.

method.description: plan.analysis, plus family_size (the number of primary metrics), the pairs planned, the fewest usable pairs of a primary metric, and min_adjusted_p: the smallest corrected p-value any primary metric's pairs allow.

outcomes.description: How many metrics got each verdict, primary and secondary apart.

noise_floor.description: From the A/A pairs (side A twice): how far two rounds of one image land apart. null when the run had no A/A pairs.

median_abs_change.description: exp(median |log ratio|) - 1 over the A/A pairs: the typical relative change between two rounds of one image.

status.description: status.json in ConfigMap compare-<run id> (labels app.kubernetes.io/component=compare-run and compare-run-id=<run id>), next to result.json (the whole results file, left out above about 900 kB). Rewritten after every round; written by summary.status.

completed_pairs.description: Scored pairs with both rounds run (ok or failed).

levels_unusable.description: Load levels of finished rounds left out of the comparison because requests failed there, or none finished.

eta_seconds.description: While running: the mean round length so far times the rounds left; otherwise null.

results_file.description: The results file's path under the results root.
